title: How to Stop Doomscrolling: 10 Ways to Break the Habit and Protect Your Mental Wellbeing
summary: Learn how to stop doomscrolling with 10 practical tips to manage negative news, reduce screen time and protect your mental wellbeing.

# How To Stop Doomscrolling – 10 Ways


You might have just picked up your phone to check a quick news update, however, you soon find yourself scrolling through more and more worrying headlines, negative videos and comments. As a result you may feel more stressed and anxious, yet strangely struggle to put your phone down.


This is often referred to as ‘doomscrolling’. It refers to continually scrolling through negative or worrying content online, leaving you feeling tense, overwhelmed and exhausted.


Whilst you don’t need to avoid the news or remove all social media apps, the aim is to be more mindful and aware of how much, when and what content you consume.


## What Is Doomscrolling?


Doomscrolling refers to when you find yourself scrolling through negative news, worrying stories or distressing content on social media. This can happen when you’re catching up on news, late at night, or simply because you opened up an app.


This is different to being mindful whilst catching up on news. Doomscrolling will be when you become stuck in a cycle of scrolling.


## How Can Doomscrolling Affect Your Mental Wellbeing?


A 2026 review looked at 44 reports of doomscrolling and its impact on mental wellbeing. It found that there were links between doomscrolling and anxiety, depression, psychological distress and reduced wellbeing. However, the researchers highlighted there was very low confidence in the evidence and this does not prove doomscrolling will cause these issues.


Everyone may have different reactions to online content. However, if you are noticing you are becoming more stressed by continuously scrolling through negative content then it may be helpful to make some changes to your feed.


### 1. Increase Feelings Of Anxiety


By continuously scrolling through content relating to threats, arguments and worrying situations you may become fixated on the problems. You may feel the need to keep checking for updates, yet there may be nothing useful you can do with the information.


### 2. Difficult To Stop Scrolling


Many apps don’t have set points for when scrolling should end. This can cause you to get caught up in one story after another and forget what time it is.


### 3. Interrupts Your Evening Routine


Checking for worrying updates late at night can keep your brain active. If you regularly find yourself scrolling late into the evening set a clear time to put your phone down.


## 10 Ways To Stop Doomscrolling


### 1. Be Mindful Of Why You Are Scrolling


Are you opening a news or social media app because you are bored, anxious, avoiding a task? By being aware of why you’re scrolling you can decide what to do instead. You could try keeping a log of when you do this for a few days to see if there are any patterns.


### 2. Set A Time For Updates


Rather than scrolling throughout the day set a specific time to catch up. Use trusted news sources and decide what you actually need to know. As soon as you’ve found the information you needed close the app.


You don’t need to be scrolling through every update to stay informed.


### 3. Disable Unnecessary Alerts


By having alerts for breaking news, trending stories and continual reminders from apps, it can cause you to go back onto your feed. Review your alert settings and disable those that aren’t important to you.


However, ensure you have your important calls, messages and safety alerts turned on.


### 4. Set Times/Places To Avoid Using Your Phone


Try setting certain times throughout the day when you won’t be browsing news/social media. For example, when eating, talking, studying or getting ready for bed.


You can also try putting your phone in another room whilst completing a task. By having some distance it can make scrolling less convenient.


### 5. Set A Time Limit On News/Social Media Apps


Use your devices time management feature to set a Time Limit on apps that have caused you to scroll. Whilst this isn’t a complete solution it can remind you to take a break.


For more tips on changing your feed, view our guide on[how to reset your social media feed](https://blockerx.net/blog/how-to-reset-your-social-media-feed/) .


### 6. Be Selective With Your Feed


Unfollow, mute or hide accounts that are constantly posting content that is causing you distress, yet isn’t providing useful information. Make use of the tools on your platform (such as ‘Not Interested’) to avoid recommendations.


Ensure you are following a variety of trustworthy sources.


### 7. Avoid Scrolling Before Bed


Try to avoid using your phone in the last part of your evening. Charge your phone away from your bed and if possible have a separate alarm clock. Try doing something calming such as reading or listening to music.


If you regularly struggle to sleep view the[CDC sleep guidelines](https://www.cdc.gov/sleep/about/) for general advice on healthy sleeping habits.


### 8. Have A Specific Task To Do


If you don’t have anything set up to help you avoid doomscrolling it can be hard to stop. Choose something simple to do.


- Go for a short walk.
- Read a few pages of a book.
- Listen to music/podcast.
- Message or talk to someone you trust.
- Complete a quick task you’ve been putting off.


Choose something that suits the time. You don’t need to make your breaks productive, taking a break and connecting with others are great alternatives.


### 9. Take A Break And Reflect


Ask yourself if the information you are viewing is useful. Does it affect any decisions you need to make? How are you feeling? If you are feeling more tense/distressed close the app and take a break.


You can still stay informed without constantly viewing the same negative information.


### 10. Make Use Of Digital Tools


Apps with time limits, focus features and website blockers can help you to stick to your boundaries.[BlockerX](https://blockerx.net/) can help users manage their access to specific online content depending on their device and features.


These should be used as a support tool. Ensure you set realistic boundaries.


## Simple Tips To Help If You Find Yourself Doomscrolling


- **Pause** – Be aware you are scrolling mindlessly.
- **Close** – Close your feed.
- **Reflect** – Ask yourself if there is any specific update you actually need.
- **Do Something** – Get back on task, take a break or connect with someone.
- **Set A Boundary** – Decide when you’ll next check the news.


## When Should I Seek Further Help?


If you’re regularly struggling with your sleep, focus, relationships or daily tasks due to online content consider speaking to a qualified mental health professional. Particularly if you are experiencing ongoing anxiety or low mood.


Don’t wait until things feel unmanageable.


## FAQs


### What Is Doomscrolling?


Doomscrolling refers to continuously scrolling through negative or worrying content online. Often you will continue to do this even if it’s not useful or making you feel worse.


### Why Am I Continuously Doomscrolling Even Though It Makes Me Anxious?


Automatically scrolling, being curious, uncertainty and the ease of continually receiving updates can make it difficult to stop. Becoming aware of what is causing you to scroll and setting a specific time to check updates can help.


### Is Doomscrolling Bad For My Mental Wellbeing?


Research has found links between doomscrolling and various aspects of mental wellbeing including anxiety. However, current evidence doesn’t show that doomscrolling will directly cause these issues and everyone will experience this differently.


### How Can I Stop Doomscrolling Before Bed?


Set a specific time to stop checking news/social media. Disable any unnecessary alerts and charge your phone away from your bed. Replace scrolling with something relaxing that doesn’t require a screen.


### Should I Avoid The News Completely?


No, it can be useful to stay informed. The aim is to choose trusted sources and be mindful when checking updates.


## Final Thoughts


Learning how to stop doomscrolling doesn’t mean you’re ignoring what is going on in the world. It simply means choosing how much information you need. By setting boundaries you can protect your time and focus.


Start with one simple change. Disable unnecessary alerts, set a time to check updates or keep your phone away in the last part of the evening. Small boundaries can help you to be more mindful with your technology.
